mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past month compresses discount rates for equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in periods where FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate economic contraction.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, or the signal's Rank IC falls below 0.03 in any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Joint growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 3-month moving averages indicates robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through increased corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 3-month moving averages, or the interaction effect's Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 4.0% YoY), a monthly CPIAUCSL increase exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals persistent inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the Fed delays rate cuts.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) in high inflation regimes when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.2pp, or the signal's Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in total nonfarm employment (PAYEMS) over the past month reflects a strengthening labor market, supporting consumer spending and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in periods of PAYEMS growth, or the signal's Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95 (2017=100) indicates manufacturing contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced corporate output and earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 95, or the signal's Rank IC < 0.03 over any 1-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous positive GDP growth (GDPC1) and rising housing starts (HOUST) above their 3-month moving averages signal a strong economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through sustained corporate profitability.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when both GDPC1 growth > 0% and HOUST > 3mo_MA, or the interaction effect's Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions (UNRATE < 4.0% and GDPC1 growth > 2.0%), a monthly decline in retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% signals weakening consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as recession risks rise.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) in late-cycle expansions when RSAFS falls > 0.5%, or the signal's Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.
